title: Anastasius: ‘adore’ need not mean latria—Moses adds ‘only’ to latria-service, not to bare adoration
source_text: VIII. Similiter Actione quarta referuntur & probantur verba Anastasii Episcopi Theopoleos, Nemo autem offendatur in adorationis vocabulo. Siquidem & homines, & sanctos Angelos adoramus, non autem quod latreian hoc est, divinum cultum exhibeamus. Inquit enim Moses: Deum tuum adorabis, & illi soli latreian praestabis: quo loco diligenter observabis, qua ratione posteriori dicto, nimirum Latriae, adjecit soli, adorabis vero, hoc ipsum non est appositum. Quamobrem adorare licet: Latria vero nequaquam: neque etiam licebit proskunein quod est proprie Deum adorare.
pass_a_gloss: Likewise in the fourth Action the words of Anastasius Bishop of Theopolis are related and approved: But let no one take offense at the vocabulary of adoration. Since indeed we also adore men and holy Angels, yet not so as to exhibit latreian, that is, divine cult. For Moses says: You shall adore your God, and to him alone you shall render latreian: in which place you will carefully observe by what reason to the latter saying, namely to Latria, he added ‘alone,’ but to ‘you shall adore’ this itself is not attached. Wherefore it is lawful to adore: but Latria by no means: nor will it even be lawful to proskunein which is properly to adore God.
pass_b_english: Anastasius: do not stumble at the word ‘adore’—we even ‘adore’ men and angels without giving divine latria.
Moses’ ‘alone’ (Deuteronomy 6:13; Matthew 4:10) binds latria-service to God, not the bare verb ‘adore.’

choices.why: Scripture’s ‘only’ is tied to latria, licensing a lesser ‘adoration’ of creatures/images.

bible_refs.note: Moses: adore God; latria to Him alone
